title: General ooRexx Deployment durable continuity corpus

records.rule: Deployment reconciles desired state with observed target state; installation is only one possible action.
Deployment never weakens application meaning to accommodate a target; it changes the target, selects another permitted strategy, or fails.
discover, assess, plan, apply and verify are distinct; only apply mutates.
Successful commands are not deployment success; fresh observed state must satisfy the manifest.
targetId is opaque and must not be equated with hostname, IP address or worker name.
Capabilities are observations; requirements are desired-state declarations.
A requirement that cannot be tested must not masquerade as verified state.
OS/package/transport mechanics belong behind providers, not hard-coded application branches.
Changing Local/SSH/container/cloud-agent transport must not change desired state.
Managed SSH configuration can invalidate a direct SSH helper; swap provider/transport while preserving hashes, plan and verification.
A generation name/marker is not authority; rehash actual content before reuse.
Content-addressed reconciliation must repair drift/corruption rather than trust stale markers.
Accept a native artifact by target load/use probe, not filename equality, controller ABI or GLIBC heuristic alone.
If the target probe fails and policy permits, rebuild from supplied source on the target and rerun the same probe.
A loader-path change is not an ABI repair.
Deployment must be able to stage the runtime that runs application code; a minimal pre-ooRexx bootstrap is allowed.
Prefer the explicitly staged executable over ambient PATH when the manifest defines one, and record the resolved path.
Hosted success is staged -> package-loadable -> composed -> activated -> live-probed.
Files beside a server are not a deployed/live module.
HTTPS Server v0.4.4 route activation is compose-before-start because routes are immutable after listener start.
An ooRexx module must directly require the package that exports classes it references; sibling package imports do not grant visibility.
MCP and Wire share the hosted-module lifecycle; protocol-specific details belong in adapter declarations.
Requirements state what must be true; deployment policy states which strategies may be used.
Model privilege explicitly; never casually prepend sudo.
Missing provenance, failed hash, incompatible architecture/runtime or failed verification blocks deployment.
Secrets are transient inputs and must not be copied into ordinary deployment evidence.
Readiness/repair and process launch are separate; start is explicit.
A similar command line is not sufficient evidence of RUNNING_EXPECTED.
Retain intent, discovery, plan, actions, observed hashes/versions/paths, final discovery and verification.
Rollback is evidence-driven and may be unavailable; reversibility must be explicit before execution.
Independent targets may reconcile concurrently with distinct DeploymentResult objects.
Same target + generation + repair key must be single-flight; concurrent callers join/observe rather than launch duplicate mutating rebuilds.
BUILDING/PREPARING is not READY; timeout or termination cannot promote readiness.
Audio V9 is the first heterogeneous proof, not a source of Audio-specific behavior for core Deployment.
Application-declared corpus/hash verification can block READY even when package staging itself succeeded.
Hosted-module qualification must include the real host/package boundary and live probe, not only fake-host unit tests.
Current executable authority is oorexx_deployment_v0.1-dev3.zip SHA-256 796b4375b7abac6e13e5f23f632c8aa75f86fe777f3d7c130ea8e440ff5dbd79; SSC identity OorexxDeployment/MAIN/sourceLevel 1.
Keep the Deployment Gopher sphere separate from the executable package and update it whenever architecture, accepted baseline or hard-won operational lessons change.
Resolve and lock declared component dependencies before Deployment plans any target mutation.
Use Semantic Source Control as ooRexx semantic dependency authority; Deployment consumes SSC rather than inventing a second source-level system.
@source-requires AT_LEAST is semantic component/surface authority; ::requires is package-load authority; preserve both separately.
Start production dependency closure from explicit deployment entry packages so tests/examples do not become dependencies merely by sharing a ZIP.
SSC_MANIFEST component/lineage/sourceLevel is authoritative; never infer sourceLevel from ZIP names, marketing versions or timestamps.
A cross-component ::requires should be backed by active @source-requires or an explicit equivalent component requirement; otherwise fail closed by default.
Emit a durable lock that records semantic component binding separately from exact package-file binding and reuse that lock for plan/apply evidence.
REXX_PATH is explicit execution state and evidence, not a semantic dependency resolver or version authority.
Passing SSC AT_LEAST proves only the known minimum; later semantic compatibility/impact qualification and application verification remain separate.
Keep the SSC dependency resolver optional so minimal ooRexx/Deployment bootstrap does not become circular.
For MCP/Wire hosted modules: resolve/lock dependencies -> materialise closure -> package-loadable -> composed -> activated -> live-probed.
Missing/duplicate component identity, lineage mismatch, insufficient/unknown source level, unresolved/ambiguous package file or unversioned cross-component require blocks resolution.
For production releases represented in current SSC, use a QUALIFIED sealed module deployment and its exact transitive ssc_deployment_dependency ids; do not float providers during Deployment.

source.get_package/latest-accepted development resolution may float under SSC policy; source.get_deployment_package/getDeploymentPackage for a sealed release must reproduce the exact qualified closure.
SSC determines which semantic bytes belong to the release; Deployment separately materialises those bytes into a deterministic target namespace and records that namespace receipt.
Materialise only explicit entry packages and reachable locked dependency files unless the whole archive is explicitly declared as the deployable artifact.
A component root whose observed artifact/content hash differs from the dependency lock or sealed receipt is a substituted provider and must fail before namespace publication.

For a locked generation, generated REXX_PATH replaces ambient REXX_PATH unless separately verified external roots are explicitly declared; package-load qualification and final launch use the same path.
Rasen Falcon LDAP identity role packages the owned LDAP tree plus an already verified exact dependency namespace; Deployment does not acquire LDAP, authorization, TLS or secret authority.
Production ooRexx service units must launch through a namespace-verifying seam that replaces ambient REXX_PATH with the exact materialised namespace before exec.

Rasen Falcon NOC and Office private mTLS endpoints are separate services named rasenfalcon-noc-https.service and rasenfalcon-office-https.service; a generic rasenfalcon-https.service must not substitute for either role.
